headline: Veto override of fiscal 2027 pay grade steps failed 7-4; $750,000 for library renovation sent to Finance Committee.
summary: Several residents spoke against a proposed trash fee during public comment. Officials presented five trash and recycling options, and more public outreach is planned. Petitions on Westminster Street properties, Laurel Hill Cemetery, and zoning moratoriums on battery storage and data centers were sent to committees.
decisions: Accepted the Appointments Committee report, including five special police officers and Robert J. Talbot to the Trustees of Public Burial Grounds, 11-0.
Adopted the minutes of the September 2, 2026 council meeting, 11-0.
Referred appointment letters for five full-time student police officers to the Appointments Committee.
Referred the memorandum of agreement with the Fitchburg Police Dispatchers Union to the Finance Committee.
Approved the Legislative Affairs Committee report on the request to repeal Chapter 164, Sales of Tobacco Products, 11-0.
Referred a $42,384 appropriation from reserve for other municipal purposes to the Finance Committee.
Referred a $4,716 appropriation from airport receipts reserved to the Finance Committee.
Referred a $750,000 appropriation for the Fitchburg Public Library renovation to the Finance Committee.
Sent the Birch Street Passway no-parking ordinance to a first and second reading and ordered it advertised, 11-0.
Referred the request to declare 465 and 0 Westminster St surplus and sell them through an RFP process to City Property.
Referred the petition to designate Ross Street and Flat Rock Road as Scenic Roads to City Property.
Referred the request to declare Laurel Hill Cemetery Parcel A surplus and sell it through an RFP process to City Property.
Referred the request for a temporary zoning moratorium on commercial battery energy storage systems to Legislative Affairs.
Referred the request for a temporary zoning moratorium on large-scale data centers to Legislative Affairs.
Referred the request to install a berm at 508 Milk Street to Public Works.
Failed to override the mayor's veto of the fiscal 2027 grade steps ordinance, roll call 7-4, so the veto stands.

City of Fitchburg  
                             Massachusetts 01420  
 
                     CITY COUNCIL  
            
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Fitchburg was held at the Legislative Building 
at 700 Main Street and over the Zoom meeting platform and live streamed at FATV Studios, 
Fitchburg, on September 15, 2026.   
 
The meeting was called to orde r by President Zarrella at 7:02 P.M.  The meeting opened with a 
salute to the Flag led by Councilor Bowen. The City Clerk called the roll 11 Councilors were present. 
Board consists of 11 members.  
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
I. PUBLIC FORUM 
  
• Bernie Stephens, Fitchburg resident, spoke regarding the proposed trash tax and its impact 
on Bridle Cross Road residents, who currently pay privately for trash and recycling 
services. He asked how the proposed trash tax would apply to the development. 
 
• Jacquelyn Wethje, Fitchburg resident, spoke in opposition to the proposed trash fee, 
expressing concerns about its use as a new revenue source and the proposed changes to 
oversight of the funds. She stated that residents should have the ability to opt out if they 
have alternative means of waste disposal.  
 
• Dr. Kendra- Sullivan Godin, Fitchburg resident, spoke in opposition to the proposed trash 
fee, citing concerns with delayed trash collection and the additional cost for residents who 
use the City dump. She also raised concerns about improper use of dumping bins and the 
financial impact of increasing fees and taxes on retired and fixed-income residents. 
 
• Jean Raabe, Fitchburg resident, spoke in opposition to the proposed trash fee, expressing 
concern about its financial impact on seniors and residents living on fixed incomes. She 
also raised concerns about the increasing cost of living and the potential for residents to 
leave Massachusetts due to rising expenses. 
 
• Carrie-Ann Knight, Fitchburg resident, spoke regarding the proposed trash fee and the 
projected increase in residential trash costs following the closure of the landfill. She 
expressed concerns about placing additional costs on taxpayers and suggested utilizing 
existing City infrastructure, including landfill gas, biomass, and an anaerobic digester, to 
generate revenue and reduce waste-related costs. 
Councilors at Large 
    Sally H. Cragin 
Amy L. Green 
Kevin T. Starr  
Elizabeth R. Walsh 
Anthony M. Zarrella 
 
President 
Anthony M. Zarrella 
 
Vice President 
Derrick J. Cruz 
         Ward Councilors 
   Ward 1 – Bernard J. Schultz III 
   Ward 2 – Paul R. Beauchemin 
   Ward 3 – Joseph S. Bowen, Jr. 
   Ward 4 – Andrew J. Van Hazinga 
   Ward 5 – Marisa R. Fleming 
   Ward 6 – Derrick J. Cruz
• Mike Couture, Fitchburg resident, spoke in opposition to additional fees and taxes, 
including the proposed trash fee. He stated that he uses a City dump permit and expressed 
concern that the proposed fee would create an additional financial burden for residents. 
 
• Jody Joseph, Fitchburg resident, former Legal Councilor, spoke in opposition to the 
proposed trash fee. He referenced a previous proposal for a trash tax that was not approved 
and urged the City to focus on controlling administrative costs rather than increasing taxes 
or fees. He also noted that the landfill has been expected to close for many years and 
questioned the need for additional costs to residents. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
II. ANNOUNCEMENTS 
The next two meetings of the Widowed Helping Widowed Support Group will take place on 
Thursday, September 17 and on Thursday, October 1 from 4 until 5:30 p.m. in Room 205 at the 
Fitchburg State University Recreation Center, 130 North Street.  Kelley Lynn, Kathy Boisvert, and 
Bernie Schultz will co-facilitate the meeting. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
Fitchburg City Councilor Bernie Schultz is hosting a City Council Community Meeting on 
Thursday, September 17, 2026 at 6:30 p.m. right here in the Legislative Building, 700 Main Street.  
Health Director Steve Curry and Irene Congdon, Municipal Assistance Coordinator from the 
Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection, will make a presentation on trash and 
recycling issues, and then answer questions following their presentation. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
The Fitchburg Historical Society is revving up its programming this fall.  
We are starting with our Annual Meeting, which is fully open to the public and will be taking place 
on Thursday, September 24, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. These meetings are historic events themselves! 
They have been going on for over 100 years, and today's residents are invited to take part in the 
tradition. It’s a great chance to meet the board members and Historical Society members, 
volunteers and staff. The annual meeting will take place at the Historic Phoenix Building, at 781 
Main Street. For more information, visit the website at Fitchburg historical society dot com.  
 
The public is also invited to the Historical Society for a talk by author Chris Boucher, who will 
speak on Harry Bucky Lew, Basketball's first Black pro and Fitchburg's role in the integration of 
Pro Sports. The talk will take place on Thursday, October 1 at 6 p.m. and is free to the public. 
Bucky Lew's mother was from Fitchburg and his grandparents came to Fitchburg from the South 
during the Civil War.  
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Fitchburg invites you to attend a highly informative, free Small Business Workshop: “Focus on 
Marketing” event occurring on Mon. Sept. 21st (6:00-7:30PM) at Fitchburg City Hall (718 Main 
St. 3rd floor).  
  
The session will provide local business owners as well as aspiring entrepreneurs with useful 
guidance on the latest approaches to effectively capture your targeted customers to grow your 
business.  Features speakers include a series of marketing experts who will share insights on the 
range of tools and approaches being utilized by today’s successful businesses.  Don’t miss this 
opportunity to learn timely information while also being able to connect with your peers within the 
local business community.
Space will be limited for this popular topic. Please contact Mary Jo Bohart – Economic 
Development Director at 978-829-1896 or email: mbohart@fitchburgma.gov 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
September 20, 2026, starting at 2 PM the acclaimed local ensemble, the Thurston consort returns 
to perform at Forest Hill Abbey also known as the Mausoleum. The Abbey’s marble interior and 
intimate setting makes for unique musical experience for all. Admission is free and donations 
accepted. These programs are supported by the Fitchburg Cultural Council. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
FITCHBURG – Calling all pets ! Second Chance Animal Services of E. Brookfield announces the 
Fall « Jeffrey P. Stephens » Low-Cost Pet Vaccine Clinic to be held at Fitchburg Fire Department, 
33  North Street, Saturday, October 3, 2026, 9 am to 1 pm. 
 
• Rabies Vaccine is just $19  
• Microchip just twenty  $20 
• Distemper and Parvo Combo Vaccine is FREE 
 
Fitchburg City Clerk will be present, and Fitchburg residents can obtain their dog license on the 
same day. The Clinic is open to residents of ANY community.  
 
There will also be a leash exchange. Turn in your dangerous plastic retractable leash for a brand 
new nylon leash.  
 
Visit: secondchanceanimals.org to reserve a spot.  
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Sunday, October 4, 2026 starting at 2 PM you can join he friends of Fitchburg cemetery for a 
special historic walking tour entitled the poetry of the bereaved at Dean Hill cemetery. You can 
learn about the history of revolutionary soldiers and their families and hear the verses inscribed on 
the slate headstones read aloud. It’s an excellent program for youth families and seniors. 
Admission is free, but donations are accepted. After the program there will be an opportunity to 
create original drawings, paintings, and photographs of the historic site and some art supplies will 
be provided.  
For more information you can email friendsoffitchburgcemeteries@gmail.com 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
The 23rd Annual Blacksmith Art & Music Festival will be held on Saturday, September 26th, 2026 
at Riverfront Park Fitchburg, Massachusetts from 10 am until 5 pm. 
 
Coordinated by community volunteers, the Annual Fitchburg Forge-In Blacksmith Art & 
Renaissance Fest has successfully showcased artisans from New England. Since 2003 we have 
welcomed over 10,000 visitors to our festival, and we expect many more this year.  
The festival is geared toward promoting the craft of blacksmithy and the arts. The exciting Forge-
In live competition, where blacksmiths create preset projects using traditional fire and anvil 
methods, makes this an unusual event. Live music, arts and crafts vendors, and renaissance-themed 
events.

Meeting of September 2, 2026 
Oral Report

Motion and second to approve the report of the Legislative Affairs Committee by unanimous  
Consent 11/0. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 members. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
VII. SPECIAL PRESENTATION 
Stephen D. Curry – Director of Public Health 
 
Trash & Recycling Program 
 
Board of Health Presentation 
 
Director of Public Health Steve Curry, Recycling Coordinator Jean-Francois Leblanc and Irene  
Congdon of MassDEP presented an overview of the City’s current waste and recycling program 
and the anticipated financial impacts of the Fitchburg-Westminster Landfill’s potential closure.  
Five waste-reduction and funding options were presented, including pay-as-you-throw bags,  
annual/flat fees, and maintaining the current system. The presentation also addressed establishing a  
waste enterprise fund, increasing recycling and composting, public education and enforcement,  
and available MassDEP grant funding. A potential implementation date of April 5, 2027, was  
discussed. Councilors asked questions regarding costs, landfill closure timing, enforcement, larger  
residential properties, composting, and collection services. No final option was selected, and  
additional public outreach and Council discussion were anticipated. 
 
Public Reminder – 8:43 PM 
The Chair reminded the general public that members of the public may not approach the Council 
bench during a meeting. The Chair also requested that the counselor pass the document down to 
the clerk for inclusion with the meeting minutes.
